findings.claim: Unrelated change in MessagePackSecurity copy constructor removes copying of HashCollisionResistant. A cloned/derived security instance silently loses the collision-resistant setting, reverting to the default and weakening secure-by-default behavior. This is out of scope for the code-coverage requirement and is a security regression (L4 records secure-by-default history).

receipt_plan.detail: Unit test: create MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData (HashCollisionResistant true), call WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(10) which uses the copy ctor, assert HashCollisionResistant is still true. Fails at head.

findings.claim: Generated code on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework is not excluded from coverage, so the 'all generated code' requirement is only partly met. The README documents this gap. Ledger L9 says follow the requirement without recording a preference; this is a known limitation rather than a recorded decision.

receipt_plan.detail: Cite the '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK' guards in the templates and the README sentence; compare to acceptance criterion 'All generated code is decorated'.

findings.claim: The attribute is applied only to formatters and resolvers, plus the resolver's nested helper classes. Any other emitted types are not covered, so 'all generated code' depends on the test enumerating every emitted file. The test only covers one source sample (object, string-key, enum, union, resolver), so generic or nested-type formatters and other templates are unchecked.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the snapshot tests and grep all generated outputs for type declarations lacking ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, including generic and nested cases.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no setting: the templates always emit [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] (guarded by #if for netstandard2.0/.NET Framework) on all formatters, resolvers and their nested helper types, with no opt-out option.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add an opt-out setting (for example a MessagePackGeneratorResultAttribute or MSBuild property) that suppresses the attribute, or also add GeneratedCode, or emit a locally defined attribute so netstandard2.0 is covered; the templates would need a flag in the generation model and conditional emission.
